title: Rees' heroic efforts not enough to stop Decatur
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Rees' heroic efforts not enough to stop Decatur

 October 21, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 STEVENSVILLE — Kent Island High boys head soccer coach Lin Outten called Brian Rees "a hero for our team."When the Buccaneers lost starting goalie Quinn Burns to injury early this season, Rees willingly stepped forward.
"We were grateful because he's the only one with goalie experience on the team," Outten said of Rees. "And yet, not recently. It was a couple of years ago on jayvee. So we've been trying so hard to protect him, and in many ways now he's protecting us."
Whether he was jumping or hitting the dirt, lunging to his right or left, Rees protected his net for almost 50 minutes during Monday night's Bayside Conference soccer championship game against Stephen Decatur at Andy Schipul Stadium. But the senior couldn't stop everything against a Seahawks team that dominated possession and scored a pair of second-half goals for a 2-0 victory.
"Man, he played out of his mind tonight," Decatur head coach Jamie Greenwood said of Rees, who finished with 20 saves. "I mean whether (shots) were at his hands or above his head, he played absolutely phenomenal.
"That was our halftime talk," added Greenwood, who noted some of his players were getting frustrated by Rees' outstanding play. "'Like we got to keep peppering him,' and 'It's going to come.' I'm not sure how many shots we had on goal, but we had a ton."
Decatur (12-1) came within inches of taking the lead just 5 minutes into the game, when Elijah Isett banged a pair of shots off the crossbar within 60 seconds of each other. Rees made a right-handed save, then made a leaping stop at the post in the 16th minute. A diving stop with 12:20 left in the first, and another save off a corner 2 minutes before intermission kept it a scoreless stalemate.
"He's a good athlete," Outten said of Rees, who logged a shutout against defending division champion Queen Anne's on Friday to clinch the North for the Bucs (7-5-1). "But the biggest thing about this is the attitude he's brought to doing it. He's brought a willingness to play hard for us, to not dwell on mistakes, to keep trying to get better. Shutout Friday against Queen Anne's and then he has this game tonight. Back-to-back games that kid has come through for us."
But Decatur, which had a decided advantage in possession, broke through 9:23 into the second half, when Isetti set up Blake Wallace's goal for a 1-0 lead.
"We had a defensive posture for most of the game until we went down 1-0, and did not keep the ball nearly as much as we would want to," Outten said. "I think Kent Island's history is to be strong in possession. And against that Decatur team we struggled to do that. This Decatur team. … excellent."
Less than 2 minutes later, Rees dropped to his knees to make a stop, then dove and extended his right arm for yet another sparkling save.
The Seahawks though nudged their lead to 2-0 with 12:10 remaining, when Johnny Crossett crossed a ball from left wing that Jay Konyar tapped into a wide open right side of the net.
"It's been a four-year process," Greenwood said of a team that features five seniors across the middle. "They've really worked for four years to get to this point. They've worked a lot in the offseason and it shows. That's what we build on. You can't score goals if you can't possess the ball. So that's one thing we teach is patience and possession."
Greenwood also stressed to his team this was not the same Kent Island team the Seahawks blanked 5-0 in the regular season's second game.
"We knew this was going to be a better team than we faced (before)," Greenwood said. "And they were going to build and get better. And we've built and got better. When you beat a team 5-0 you've got to talk 'em down and say, 'Listen. It's not the same team, and you got to come out and play.' I thought they showed real well tonight. Lin's got a good group to head into the playoffs."
Decatur last won the Bayside in 2022, when it defeated Kent Island 5-1.

title: Lions battle but can't snap Bayside title game struggles
author: Bill Haufe

Lions battle but can't snap Bayside title game struggles

 October 21, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 STEVENSVILLE — Queen Anne's County High's girls soccer team has won 16 North Bayside titles during Mike Kern's 25-year run as head coach.As for the Bayside Conference championship? Well, that's another story.
"The Bayside is a curse," said Kern, who's teams have won the conference crown only twice.
That curse continued Monday night, as Sam Ruppert scored off a rebound with just over 10 minutes remaining in the first half, lifting Stephen Decatur to a 1-0 victory at Kent Island High's Andy Schipul Stadium, earning the Seahawks their first Bayside title since 2014.
"We played hard," Kern said of his team which had six junior varsity players dressed because injuries have plagued his team this season. "They beat us a little to the ball. We were a little out of sync. Our touches weren't the greatest tonight, but I love their effort. The effort was there and we played hard.
"They had a good opportunity, they capitalized," Kern said of the Seahawks. "We had a couple that we didn't capitalize on."
The Seahawks (11-2) capitalized in the game's 30th minute. Lions freshman goalie Hayleigh Clark made huge save, batting the ball away to her left. But Queen Anne's (12-1) couldn't clear the ball before Ruppert came in from the right side of the box and knocked the game's lone goal into the net.
"We always talk about with set pieces — corners, free kicks — it's mostly a desire," Decatur head coach Will Cooledge said. "It's mostly, 'Do you want it more than the person you're going up against?' And today I think we did."
The Lions had chances to pull even, but either just missed the mark or were denied by Seahawks goalie Harper Jerns, who intercepted Bre Kerns' cross early in the second half. Queen Anne's put a ball at the right post with 12:50 remaining but couldn't get anyone there for a shot. Bre Kerns then drove a tough angled shot over the goal with 7:20 left.
And while the Bayside has always proved a struggle for the Lions, their head coach has always had a bigger concern — injury on the cusp of the regional playoffs. And in a season where his defending Class 2A state champions have been riddled with injuries, the Lions didn't need another.
"The only thing about this game I hate is risking injuries. And now Hayleigh went out," Kern said of Clark, who has started all but one game this season after last year's starting goalie, Bea Holthaus, suffered a season-ending injury over the summer. "We'll see how long she'll be out for."
Clark was injured with 6:17 remaining, when she and Decatur's Luca Russo collided while going after a 50-50 ball. Kyra Khamvongsa finished the game in goal for Queen Anne's.
"I thought Hayleigh played a great game," Kern said. "Hayleigh made a great save (on the ball before Ruppert's goal). They made a great play. Good shot on goal. Heckuva save. We didn't get the clear and they were able to put the rebound in. That happens. But Hayleigh a couple of good saves."
Queen Anne's lost last year's Bayside game to James M. Bennett before going on to win its first state title in girls soccer, a feat Kern hopes his team can repeat despite its lengthy injury list.
"I think the girls realized what we did last year and they'll respond well," Mike Kern said.
Stephen Decatur's boys defeated Kent Island in the second game of Monday's doubleheader, giving the Seahawks their first sweep of the Bayside soccer titles in school history.
"It's exciting," said Cooledge, whose team lost its second game of the regular season to Queen Anne's. "It was a good wakeup call for us. And we were able to make adjustments early in the season and work on things we thought maybe were flaws and refine our good things. And it allowed us to change this result today."

 October 21, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Headlines

 CENTREVILLE — They weren't trying to make a fashion statement as much as they were seeking an added edge.So in August, Kent Island High's field hockey team, anchored by the senior trio of Emma Wackowski and sisters Willow and Rita Yost — who were all starting their fourth year on varsity — lobbied to bring back the uniforms they wore as freshmen.
"They said, 'We're going to wear the uniforms we wore as freshmen because we went to the state semis that year, and we want states,'" Bucs head coach Laura Harding said. "'We like them better, and they're good luck.'"
So the varsity exchanged the uniforms it had worn the past two years for the old threads. The switch has worked out pretty well so far considering Kent Island hasn't lost a game all season. The Bucs moved their win total to an even dozen Tuesday night with a 4-0 victory over Stephen Decatur at Queen Anne's County High for their first Bayside Conference championship since 2019.
"I'm excited," Harding said. "They're so much fun to coach. They're hungry. They want it."
Kent Island showed that on both ends on this beautiful October evening.
Decatur (8-4) earned three of the game's first four penalty corners. The Seahawks didn't manage a shot their first two opportunities, but got off three rapid-first attempts on their third try, only to be denied by Kent Island junior goalie Brynja Petursson, who made one save lying down and another from her knees.
"The defense is solid with Brynja back there," said Harding who watched Petursson make eight saves en route to her ninth shutout of the season. "She is a solid defender. She's got a 94 percent save percentage this year."
The group fronting Petursson has also been pretty special this year, led by the senior foursome of Wackowski, Rita Yost, Alice Phelan and Laura Peck. That group pressured the Seahawks whenever they got close to venturing into the circle Tuesday.
The Bucs (12-0) also showed their hunger on the offensive end, starting with 1:45 remaining in the first quarter, when Finley Davidson snapped a shot from 10 yards out into the cage for a 1-0 lead. Kent Island pushed that advantage to 2-0 just 1:57 into the second quarter, as Grace Mathews carried into the circle and squeezed a shot inside the right post and the left pad of Decatur goalie Kate Miller-Vail (six saves).
"They finish this year." Harding said of her offense. "They know how to put the ball in the cage which we've struggled with in the past."
Kent Island had three more penalty corners in the third, but couldn't get anything else past Miller-Vail.
But the Bucs began padding their lead early in the fourth, as Davidson converted a feed from Matthews for a goal off a corner with 12:03 left to play. Willow Yost capped the scoring, taking a feed from Anna Fronczek and scoring for the game's final tally with a little over 4 minutes remaining.
"They all play hockey year-round," Harding said. "They are field hockey players."

title: Foxx's storied baseball career started in Easton
author: MARK MILLIKIN Special to the Bay Times Record Observer
content:
Foxx's storied baseball career started in Easton

 October 20, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: MARK MILLIKIN Special to the Bay Times Record Observer | Section: Local News 
 
 1050
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It's World Series time again and the birth month of a local legend. This brings to mind my early research on native Marylander and Baseball Hall of Famer Jimmie Foxx.I made several trips to the Centreville branch of the Queen Anne's County library in 1990 and 1991, and a librarian there pointed me to the Record-Observer office across the street on Lawyer's Row. The librarian told me that the Record-Observer Office had some original copies of issues of the Centreville Observer and the Centreville Record from the early 1900s. I was most interested in any information about Jimmie Foxx's playing in scholastic sports for Sudlersville High School and town baseball.
From the start of my visits to the Record-Observer, office manager Dorothy Monroe was very cordial and happy to help me with my project. It was just before we had smart phones with cameras, so I had to take many handwritten notes, but it was well worth the time I spent there. It was exhilarating to me as a researcher to stumble upon so much valuable information about the early life of Jimmie Foxx.
These local first-hand accounts about the pride that friends, family and other sports fans in the County felt for Foxx were unique. They were genuine and believable. Those issues of the County's newspapers were also a goldmine of information for me about Foxx's early participation in sports that could not have been found elsewhere, enabling me to ground truth the fact that Jimmie was a very versatile, well-rounded athlete with extraordinary strength, speed and agility when he was a teenager.
Many accounts in the Observer and Record in 1922 and 1923 mentioned Foxx in brief notes and box scores. Another thrilling aspect for me during that research was to read quotes presumably written by those papers' sports editors (among them Vach Downes and Jack Wesley) that expressed the excitement that they and many sports fans in the County were feeling about Foxx's sports exploits, especially in baseball and track and field.
I had read in more recent stories about Foxx that he starred in many sports in the early 1920s, but now I was poring over many weekly issues of those two papers from 1921-1924 that gave specifics on his superb playing of baseball, volleyball, soccer, basketball, track and field and speedball for Sudlersville High, and his starring role, even as a young teen in town baseball, mostly for Sudlersville against other nearby town teams.
The Easton Farmers professional baseball club was organized for the 1924 season and hired Trappe native Frank "Home Run" Baker, former standout slugger of the Philadelphia A's and New York Yankees, as their manager.
The timing of that team's formation could not have been better for Jimmie Foxx's baseball career. The May 3, 1924, issue of the Observer proudly announced, "Master James Foxx, son of Mr. and Mrs. Dell Foxx has signed up with manager Frank Baker of the Easton team in the Eastern Shore League. He will leave about the 16th for a preliminary workout."
Now that Foxx was playing for Easton for the summer of 1924, his baseball career was also being covered by Easton newspapers, but all of them spelled his last name with one "x" at the end.
Meanwhile, other information about Jimmie's athletic career at Sudlersville High kept appearing in the Observer. Its June 28, 1924 issue included a photo of the "[1923] Sudlersville Soccer Ball Champions" with "James Foxx" seated on the bottom row by himself (holding a soccer ball; he was the team captain), his teammates standing behind him and Harry Rasin, coach. The following week, the July 5 issue included a photo of the "[1923] Sudlersville Basketball Champions," James Foxx seated in the center, holding the ball (Harry Rasin, coach). In the July 5 issue, the Observer wrote in an editorial, "Why not a Queen Anne's County Day at Easton in honor of [Alton] Scott and Foxx (when they are scheduled to play)?"
The Easton club responded quickly to the Observer. In its July 12 issue, the Observer told its readers, "Next Wednesday will be "Queen Anne's Day at Easton. Manager Baker has picked Scott to pitch and Foxx to catch — local fans expected in force." The Observer also noted, "every day, scores of automobile loads of Queen Anne's County fans follow the teams about the [Eastern Shore League] circuit, but when the Farmers play on their home field, there is a mass exodus of fans from every corner of the County."
The Observer noted in its July 19 issue, "about 400 to 500 Queen Anne's County residents showed up for the Queen Anne's County Day at Federal Park…only to see Dover drop Easton, 10-8." An article reported, "In the second, Foxx slammed a triple and scored Easton's first run. In the ninth, he pounded the horsehide over the left field fence for possibly the longest homer of the season."
Jimmie Foxx reached a new landmark in his budding baseball career just three months after joining Baker's Easton Farmers when he was purchased by major league manager Connie Mack (Philadelphia A's) through scout Mike Drennan from Frank Baker's Easton Farmers on July 30. The Aug. 2 issue of the Observer proclaimed in its article, "Athletics Scout Buys Jimmy Foxx from Easton Club," "For the first time in the history of organized baseball, Queen Anne's County is to contribute a baseball player to the major leagues. He is Jimmy Foxx, son of Mr. and Mrs. Dell Foxx, of near Sudlersville, who this week was purchased by scout Mike Drennan, representing Connie Mack of the Philadelphia Athletics." The article noted Foxx will complete the season with Frank Baker first.
Now the talk of baseball fans on the Eastern Shore baseball fans who regarded Jimmie Foxx as their favorite player revolved around the possibility that he might be playing for the A's soon and fans could motor to the A's home park of Shibe Park in Philadelphia to see him play in person. Too, this possibility had a tremendous amount of appeal to Dell Foxx and his brothers-in-law.
On Judge Landis Day in Easton (Aug. 15) the Observer noted in its Aug. 23 issue, "Foxx landed on the horsehide and rode it over the center field fence. Judge Landis, National Baseball Commissioner gave the Sudlersville lad an enthusiastic hand as he trotted home with the four-base tally."

title: Seahawks rally, then hold off Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Seahawks rally, then hold off Easton

 October 17, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Matt Griffith checked his simmering emotions, but was convinced nonetheless."It was pass interference," Easton High's head football coach said without hesitation of a no-call on his team's third-to-last offensive play of the game.
Griffith though conceded, "While it was PI, there were things we could have controlled during the game on both sides of the ball that doesn't leave us in that situation."
The Warriors' offensive line was physical. Sophomore running back Jamier Copper had a career night. And freshman quarterback Nicky O'Connor stood tall in his first varsity start. But that combination wasn't enough to defeat two-time defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur Friday night, as Kyle Mumford ran for two touchdowns and had a pair of TD receptions in a 28-25 victory over Easton.
"If they had won the game, unquestionably, their o-line and (Copper) would have gotten game balls," Stephen Decatur head coach Jake Coleman said after his team's fifth consecutive victory. "Their offensive line deserves a ton of credit, and obviously the freshman (O'Connor) coming in there. But Copper was ridiculous. He ran like a grown man tonight."
Copper carried 39 times for 247 yards — both season-highs — and had two touchdowns runs, the second, a 21-yarder that pulled the Warriors (5-2) within 21-19 with 9 minutes, 17 seconds remaining in the third quarter.
Easton then took its first lead at 25-21 with 8:52 left in the game, when O'Connor, starting for the injured Brady Walls, hit Kyree Acree on the sideline for a 19-yard touchdown pass. O'Connor (9 of 22, 110 yards) tried running in the two-point conversion but was stopped short.
After both teams exchanged punts, Decatur (5-1) took over on its 41-yard line with 3:15 remaining. Quarterback Johnny Hobgood (10 of 13, 110 yards, two touchdowns) threw a 14-yard completion. Mumford picked up three. Easton was then flagged for pass interference, giving the Seahawks a first down at the Easton 27. Two plays later, Mumford (16 carries, 98 yards) bolted through the middle for a 23-yard touchdown with 1:53 left. Blake Wallace booted his fourth extra point for a 28-25 lead.
"You go on the road against a really good team, a team that was beating us physically quite honestly, and to be able to hang in there and not give up, and keep playing through it. … " Coleman said. "Those are different boxes you have to check. Can you come from behind? Can you go on the road against a good team? Can you be getting punched in the mouth then withstand that and stay in it? Those are questions I think every team has to answer. And I think we answered that question."
Easton got the ball back one last time. On third-and-10 from its 23, O'Connor hit Carter Mooney, who lateraled to Logan Friend for a 22-yard pickup. O'Connor found Acree for 12 yards to the Decatur 43. The Seahawks were flagged for pass interference on the next play, giving Easton first down at the 28 with 1:08 left.
Copper was dropped for a 5-yard loss on first down. Then on second down, O'Connor threw toward Mooney. Decatur's defender made contact with the Easton receiver but no flag was thrown, prompting protest from the Warrior sideline.
"You can't not make that call when the game's on the line," Griffith said. "That puts us in field goal range. We've already hit two from there."
O'Connor was sacked for a 6-yard loss on third down before throwing incomplete on fourth.
Hobgood dropped to a knee twice to kill the remaining 42 seconds on the clock.
"Offensive line, Jamier and Nicky O'Connor," Griffith said. "Got a freshman playing quarterback put in a tough situation against a really good football team, and I thought they were outstanding for most of the night. Decatur's well-coached. They (Decatur) made enough plays at the right time that they ended up coming out on top tonight."
Decatur took a 7-0 lead just 1:22 into the game, when Hobgood hit Mumford for a 30-yard touchdown pass.
Luke Stanco hit field goals of 23 and 31 yards to draw the Warriors within 7-6 with just over 4 minutes left in the first quarter. Mumford's 13-yard touchdown run with 2:34 to go in the opening quarter expanded the Seahawks' lead to 14-6.
Easton responded with Copper scoring on a 7-yard run with 5:25 left in the first half. Stanco's kick made it a 14-13 game. Decatur again widened its lead, with Hobgood and Mumford teaming for an 11-yard scoring play with 1:14 left in the half.
The Warriors cut that deficit to 21-19 in the third, with Copper carrying six times on a seven-play, 66-yard scoring march that ended with his 21-yard touchdown run.
"I think Copper unquestionably is one of the most underrated players in the conference," Coleman said. "And the thing that I appreciate about him is the tough yards. When we had him wrapped up he always fought for two or three more. He was a hammer.
"And that O'Connor kid, oh my goodness," Coleman added. "I think when our guys initially saw him we were kind of like, 'Oh, man. We're facing a freshman quarterback.' Man, he did not look like it today."

title: One proves enough for Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
One proves enough for Easton

 October 16, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — Both coaches obviously wanted victory, and after 80 minutes of heated, physical play in the latest installment of the Easton-St. Michaels High soccer rivalry, Warrior head coach Avery Brice breathed a sigh of relief as his team continued its late-season surge."Good game. One-oh. Got the result," Brice said after Rodrigo Fresco's goal in the fifth minute Wednesday night proved enough for a 1-0 Easton victory over the Saints.
And though St. Michaels suffered its fourth loss in five games, Saints head coach Pat Hambleton may have gotten something he was looking for as well — momentum.
"We've had a hard stretch," Hambleton said after his team's third one-goal loss in 10 days, which included a 3-2 double-overtime defeat to two-time defending North Bayside champion Queen Anne's County. "I asked them, 'Just give us momentum. Create momentum so we can move forward. Win, lose, draw, figure out a way to play well. Work hard. Find something to carry on for tomorrow (a 9-0 victory Thursday over Cambridge-South Dorchester) and then carry on into the playoffs.'"
The Saints (6-4-1 overall, 2-4-1 North Bayside) may have found that momentum, playing the game's last 35 minutes, 54 seconds a man down after one of its players received a red card while an Easton player was given a yellow.
"I thought down (to) 10 men, I felt like we had the upper hand, and I felt like we were the man up," said Hambleton, who argued Easton should have also received a red.
"Couldn't be more proud," Hambleton added of his team. "We took them out of their game. They were sitting six guys in the back for the last 20 minutes terrified of our attack and our pressure. And I thought the second half was a completely different game than the first half."
With 4:28 elapsed in the first half, Fresco got a ball on the right side and parked it past Saints keeper Lucas Greenwood for the game's lone goal and a 1-0 Warrior lead.
The remainder of the game featured a string of highlight-reel saves by Greenwood (10 saves) and Easton goalie Sam Hutchison (eight saves).
Greenwood leaped to punch a ball away with 26:10 remaining in the first half. Hutchison stopped St. Michaels' Abel Delgaudio just 50 seconds later. Greenwood lunged left to foil Luke Stanco a little over 5 minutes later. St. Michaels' Connor Wheeler then struck a direct kick that Hutchison reached before colliding with Delgaudio. Greenwood made another stop a moment later, and Hutchsion responded with another save before a second collision 5 minutes later, leaving Brice pleading with his team, "You need to wake up."
The game was mostly played between the 18s in the second half, though both keepers continued to come up big. Easton had a chance to pad its lead 9 minutes into the half, but Emmet Fox drove a shot off the left post. Hutchison picked up another save, when he knocked away a ball on a Saints corner. Greenwood maintained the one-goal difference, smothering a ball off a wild scramble with an Easton player leaping over him.
"We just need to be consistent in the back and then take care of the ball a little bit better," said Brice, his team 6-5, 6-2 after its fourth win in five games.
For Hambleton, it was a familiar theme.
"The story of the second half of our season is we're winning games off the scoreboard," Hambleton said. "And that doesn't count."

title: Lions win North as Kern gets milestone
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions win North as Kern gets milestone

 October 16, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 510

 Read News Document

 Lexi and Bre Kern knew of their father's approaching milestone, and may have even told a few teammates.But Queen Anne's County High girls head soccer coach Mike Kern said nothing to his team that he was closing on 300 career wins.
The Lions' head coach of 25 years had serious doubts about that mark this season, considering starters Bea Holthaus, Madi Horney, Abby Robinson and Rilynn Hesson had all been lost to knee injuries. Those four injuries also gave Kern reason to believe his defending Class 2A state champions might fall short in their bid to defend the North Bayside title.
Those doubts vanished Wednesday night. Kaylie Scearce scored one goal and set up another, and Shannon Rath served up a pair of long-distance assists to help Queen Anne's to a 3-1 victory over Kent Island in a battle of unbeatens at Andy Schipul Stadium, earning Kern his 300th career win.
The Lions (12-0 overall, 7-0 North Bayside) will face South Bayside champion Stephen Decatur on Monday at 5 p.m. for the conference championship at Kent Island.
"Honest to God I don't know how we did it. I really don't," Kern said during a phone interview Thursday. "I didn't think we were going to get by Kent Island just because of how banged up we are. I was kind of hesitant to even go that route and think that far ahead. So when it happened I was kind of shocked."
Among the reasons Kern kept quiet about the milestone was the fact Kent Island had defeated South powers James M. Bennett (7-3) and Decatur (4-1) during the regular season, while the Lions defeated both the Clippers and Seahawks by one goal.
Those concerns may have started to subside in the first half Wednesday, when Scearce crossed a ball that Marley Benson trapped and knocked into the left side of the net for a 1-0 Queen Anne's lead. That lead grew to 2-0 before halftime, as Rath booted a direct kick from the 50-yard line that cleared the pack crowded in front of the goal and landed on the foot of Kara Ringold, who deposited it into the net.
The Lions made it 3-0 early in the second half, when Rath launched another free kick from inside the 50 and watched Scearce put a head on it for a goal.
"Kent Island is fast. They're so fast," Kern said. "So we just tried to slow the game down. We knew if we were going to be up and down we were going to be in trouble. We slowed the game down, just kind of possessed, played to feet. We didn't try to outrun them or try to play the ball long. We just kept it short, build slow."

 EASTON — Debbie McQuaid has coached a lot of field hockey for a lot of years.She's led high school teams to championships and guided club teams to showcase triumphs.
But Saints Peter and Paul High's head coach quickly admitted she's never had a game quite like this.
"I don't think I've had a more exciting comeback game in all my coaching career," McQuaid said.
Freshman Caroline Corson scored two goals, including the game-winner early in the fourth quarter Friday, as the Sabres rallied from a two-goal deficit to defeat county rival Easton, 3-2, for their sixth consecutive win.
"To come back from a 2-0 deficit, and against a rival." said McQuaid after Sts. Peter & Paul improved to 8-2 via its third one-goal victory of the season. " They (Easton) played us well. They're a good team. And I'll tell you, (Easton goalie) Taylor Bowen is something."
Bowen and her defense weathered eight Sabres penalty corners through the game's first 39 minutes.
But Sts. Peter & Paul finally got on the board, when Corson scored off a corner with 6 minutes, 11 seconds remaining in the third quarter, trimming the Warriors' lead to 2-1.
"We knew we still had a bunch of time," Corson said. "I knew that we could come back from that because we don't normally like keep our heads low. We kind of just capitalize on what's going on. And we did it."
The Sabres earned two more corners before the quarter was over, but could not get a shot on the cage as Easton (6-4) maintained its one-goal edge heading into the fourth.
Angie Webb then worked through Easton's defense on the left side of the circle before crossing a pass to Kiera Crossed for the tying goal 35 seconds into the final period.
"Easton's defense held strong," McQuaid said. "I just knew it was a matter of time. If we could just settle. We were getting a little flustered. Both teams wanted to win this."
Less than 4 minutes later, Corson smacked a rising shot toward the cage. Bowen made a fine initial save, batting the ball upward with her hand. But the ball arced backward, slipping under the crossbar and into the cage for the go-ahead goal with 10:40 left in the game.
"I was just so shocked and happy," Corson said. "I was going to pass it and then I saw the open space and I just shot it. It went up and I didn't think it went in the goal. And then I heard it and everybody started cheering and I was like, 'Oh my gosh.' So good."
The Warriors' best chance to tie came a little over a minute later, when they worked a deflection off a corner that sailed over the cage.
"I have never played with a more determined team," Sabres senior standout Jules Stepp said. "We just knew the game isn't over until the clock says it is."
After a scoreless first quarter, Easton took a 1-0 lead when Ryan Quicke set up McKenna Clow's goal with 6:45 remaining before halftime. Sts. Peter & Paul earned seven corners in the second quarter alone, but couldn't slip anything past Bowen.
"I thought our defense did a great job," Easton head coach Kim Neff said. "They had a lot of corners and Taylor Bowen had some amazing saves."
The Warriors took a 2-0 lead not quite 5 minutes into the third period. After not getting a shot on goal on a corner, Quicke regained possession and fired a shot past Sabres goalie Pyper Mister.
But Mister and her defensive mates wouldn't let anything else past.
"They were not making strong passes," Neff said of her team after its third one-goal loss of the season. "They were not working as a unit that first quarter. I do feel like when we came out second half we had a more dominating quarter, and we were working together. But again, they were going back to that individual play and it didn't work."

title: New-look Sabres extend winning trend

 EASTON — His team had lost only once in nine games and was sitting atop the conference.That's when Saints Peter and Paul High first-year girls head soccer coach Josh Plugge decided it was time for a change.
"Early on we were just playing athletically; playing fast," Plugge said. "We were putting the ball either on Eden's foot or Avery's foot, and we were just playing it over the top. However, you can't win every game that way."
The Sabres transitioned more toward a game of possession, playing to feet and creating space, and promptly lost back-to-back games. Plugge refused to revert back to the old ways and has slowly seen the new game plan take shape.
That shape was at its sharpest Thursday, as Eden Zimmerman celebrated senior day with a hat trick, pacing Sts. Peter & Paul to a 4-1 victory over Worcester Prep that forged a first-place tie atop the Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference.
The defending conference champion, the Sabres improved to 10-3 overall, 7-1 ESIAC, pulling even with Gunston (8-1, 7-1) atop the ESIAC. Sts. Peter & Paul and Gunston split their two regular-season games, and may be headed for a coin flip to decide who gets the No. 1 seed and home-field advantage for the approaching conference playoffs.
"It's like we're putting together a puzzle once piece at a time," Plugge said of the new scheme. "We get this one player doing what we need them to do, and now it's like, 'OK. Next piece.' And today we were maybe one or two pieces away from just this complete puzzle.
"In terms of since this new switch in strategy, this is the best (we've played)," Plugge continued. "We put a lot of pieces together today. We played really well."
During Sts. Peter & Paul's 8-1 start to the season, Zimmerman and fellow senior Avery McCall often sent passes over defenses to forward Alicia Shanks. Sensing that attack would only last so long, Plugge shifted Zimmerman from striker to center midfield to help implement the new design. There was a tough learning curve with a 1-0 double-overtime loss to Gunston and a 3-0 loss to Cambridge-South Dorchester.
But the Sabres have become more comfortable with their new look, outscoring their past two opponents, 8-1, which included Thursday's win over the Mallards.
"We're actually playing soccer instead of just passing the ball up," Zimmerman said. "I can definitely see a huge difference. We're all passing well, getting good touches, getting the ball up. It's paying off."
It paid off again yesterday, but not before Hannah Coyle gave the Mallards a 1-0 lead with 13:30 remaining in the first half.
That only seemed to stir the Sabres offense.
A little over 3 minutes later, Zimmerman got inside the box and fired wide. Annie Albright followed moments later with another shot wide of the net. But with 5:53 left before halftime, Zimmerman gained possession on a corner kick, and with two defenders to her left, put a shot into the net for a 1-1 tie.
Just 1:16 later, Zimmerman caught up to a through ball from McCall down left wing and parked her second goal into the back of the net for a 2-1 lead that stood at the half.
"I can definitely see a ton of difference," Zimmerman said. "We have a young team and putting Alicia up top, she has good footwork and she's fast. And then utilizing the three seniors in the middle (Zimmerman, McCall and Albright), where we can all just pass together, and then just set it up is definitely working."
The Sabres kept Worcester goalie Kylee Hutton busy in the second half, but the freshman kept it a one-goal difference, stopping a low shot from McCall, watching Zimmerman clang one off the crossbar, and making a save on Shanks' sinking drive in a 5-minute window.
The puzzle clicked again though with 21:09 left, when Zimmerman got inside the box unmarked on right wing and scored, completing her hat trick for a 3-1 lead.
"I wish I would have been here for four years to coach her because the talent she is, and the talent that she has in space," Plugge said of Zimmerman. "She's one of the best players every time she steps on the field. She forces the players around her to be better."
Albright capped the scoring with 11:45 left, when she got a ball in the center of the box and scored before getting knocked to the ground.

title: Saints get even, but Lions get win
author: Bill Haufe
content:

 ST. MICHAELS — Jackson Troyer has not played a lot of minutes this year.That's certainly understandable considering the Queen Anne's County High boys soccer team's propensity for close games.
Inserted into the fray after a senior starter was injured, Troyer may have understandably been a bit nervous Monday night when he got the ball on his foot early in the second overtime with a chance to shoot.
"I whiffed the first shot," Troyer admitted.
He didn't miss the second.
The sophomore struck a shot with the outside of his foot from about 15 yards out on the right side of the box Monday night, and watched it settled into the left side of the net with 2 minutes, 53 seconds remaining in the second OT, giving the Lions a 3-2 victory over a gritty St. Michaels team.
With its sixth one-goal victory of the season — five coming against North Bayside competition — Queen Anne's improved to 7-3 overall, 6-0 division. The Lions can clinch a third straight division title with a win at Colonel Richardson (4-4-1, 1-4-1) next Monday and a victory at home next Thursday against Kent Island (5-3-1, 5-0-1).
"That's a good group of kids that Wade's put out on the field," St. Michaels head coach Pat Hambleton said of Queen Anne's and its head coach Wade Hosler.
It also looked like a group that was well on its way to a third consecutive victory.
After a scoreless first half, Nathan Kostka tucked a ball into the upper left corner in the second minute of the half for a 1-0 Lions lead. Saints keeper Lucas Greenwood kept it a one-goal game with a pair of huge point-blank stops over the next two minutes.
St. Michaels (5-2-2, 2-2-1) appeared to tie the game with 27:30 left in regulation, only to have the score negated, when the referee ruled the Saints player who crossed the ball had stepped out of bounds.
Queen Anne's nudged its lead to 2-0 Landon Nordvik gained possession down the right side, made a couple of touches, and unloaded a rocket from just outside the box that nestled into the upper left corner with 22:47 remaining in regulation.
The Lions, who entered the game having yielded just one goal all season to a North opponent (Easton), looked to be in good position for their sixth victory in seven games.
But the Saints, who learned a valuable lesson earlier in the season when their two-goal lead vanished in the final 9 minutes of regulation in an eventual 2-2 double-overtime draw with Kent Island, kept pressing.
Connor Wheeler, who consistently launched long throws all night, sent a number of throw-ins into the box. St. Michaels threatened with 17:40 but the Lions cleared. Greenwood made another close-range stop with 8 minutes remaining.
Then with 3:19 left in regulation, a St. Michaels player was fouled inside the box, setting up Gavin Bieber's penalty kick into the right side of the net, making it a 2-1 game. Just 53 seconds later on another throw-in, St. Michaels' Johnny Mautz rose above the crowd for a header that bounced into the right side of the net for a 2-2 tie.
"One thing the Kent Island game taught us is that you can score within the (final) 10 (minutes)," Hambleton said. "That's the kind of mindset we had. Once we were down two I feel like they used that."
Though St. Michaels' two goals in 53 seconds were stunning, Hosler said he wasn't stressed.
"They'd been dangerous on long throws all game and we just didn't handle it," Hosler said of St. Michaels. "We handled all of them but that one. It was a good throw and they have some tall guys. They crash hard. So it's hard to come back from that, but I thought we did.
"We responded well," Hosler added. "It was good timing to get that break between overtime and we kind of got recomposed. And we found some possession again and some chances, but didn't find it in the first."
Scoreless after the first 10-minute overtime, Wheeler opened the second extra session with a 50-yard boot that Lions keeper Braeden Livingston made a leaping stop on at the crossbar. That led to a pair of St. Michaels corners, but the Saints couldn't capitalize.

Easton ice rink picks up slack, welcomes teams after rink closure in Delaware

 EASTON — The ice rink inside of the Talbot County Community Center usually has a hefty winter schedule. This year's will be even more jam-packed.Local hockey teams and figure skaters in the Delmarva region are facing the first fall and winter seasons without the Centre Ice Rink, a facility formerly located on the Delaware State Fairgrounds in Harrington, around 45 minutes from Easton. It closed in May due to funding issues.
Many have turned to the Easton ice rink, operated by Talbot County Parks and Recreation inside of the community center on Route 50.
Jonny Brown, assistant facilities manager, said teams and clubs rushed to contact the Easton facility when the Harrington rink announced its closure in January.
"Everyone's phone was ringing with, 'What's available?'" Brown recalled.
Now, as temperatures dip and hockey season begins, Easton's rink — the only full-year rink on the Eastern Shore of Maryland — is ready for one of its busiest years yet.
Talbot Parks and Recreation Director Emily Gilmer said it was a "time-consuming" process to piece together a schedule that accommodated returning groups, new teams, open skate sessions and more.
"Normally, ice schedule's pretty much set," Gilmer said. "You've got the same user groups, they've got the same time. This year, it was like, let's just throw the entire ice schedule into a pot and just completely redo it almost."
Luckily, Gilmer said they've been able to mix and match schedules, welcoming in new teams and groups including the Delmarva Warriors and Salisbury University's ice hockey team.
The rink will also host an adult hockey league made up of 10 teams across two divisions, mostly playing games on weekend and Monday nights.
"We really didn't think we were going to be able to do it at first because we did not have a consistent time available for them," Gilmer said. But ice rink staff made it work by slightly modifying public skate times, she said.
Open skate times are still available for the public throughout the week: Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays from 1 to 3 p.m.; Fridays from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m; Saturdays from 7 to 9 p.m.; and Sundays from 1:30 to 3:30 p.m.
Brown said there will be more ice maintenance and staffing required throughout the coming weeks to handle the increased usage of the rink. He said he's started to go from once-a-week maintenance to three days a week.
In addition to his role with the parks and recreation department, Brown is president of the nonprofit Eastern Shore Hockey Association, or Easton Ice Hawks. Made up of many teams at different age levels, the group relies on Easton's ice rink for practices.
And with the Harrington closure earlier this year, many kids left teams in Delaware to join the Ice Hawks. Brown said there's around 40 or 50 kids on the team this year that came from Harrington teams or clubs.
"As an organization, we didn't want to turn anyone away," Brown said, adding that ESHA was largely able to prevent from having to make new teams. Instead, most teams are closer to the 20-member limit with the influx of kids from Delaware.
Gilmer and Brown each recognized the idea of expanding the ice rink, though they acknowledged it's a significant financial commitment.
"There's been talks about, 'Oh we should get a second sheet of ice,'" Gilmer said. "While we would love to, I'm sure that's a decent expense. I could almost guarantee that we could probably fill it, especially from September, October all the way to February."
In the meantime, Gilmer said she's excited for the busy season on the ice. She and others at the parks and recreation department will be monitoring to see how the schedule pans out in the coming months.
"We're gonna really take the numbers this year and compare to other ice rinks and what they do," Gilmer said.

 AMERICAN CORNER — Derrick Mitchell picked the perfect time to stop dancing.The senior running back ran for two touchdowns and three two-point conversions, and picked up two huge first downs on a game-sealing drive Friday night, helping Colonel Richardson High's football team to a 38-28 victory over Cambridge-South Dorchester.
"Derrick did what he needed to do," Colonel head coach James Jackson said after his team's third straight win. "'Let's not dance.' I've been trying to get him out of that all year. I've been telling him, 'Derrick, you're dancing too much.' And the second half he didn't dance. He lowered his shoulder and ran over some people."
Mitchell's 15-yard touchdown run around left end and his ensuing two-point conversion run gave Colonel (3-2) a 38-28 lead with 9 minutes, 32 seconds remaining in the game.
Cambridge-SD (0-5) looked ready to cut into that lead, driving from its 43-yard line to the Colonel 16, where on first-and-10, quarterback Nathan Twilley ran for three yards but suffered an apparent knee injury. Twilley did not return.
Viking backup quarterback TJ Wilson picked up nine yards on his first snap, giving Cambridge-SD a first-and-goal at the Colonels' 4. Wilson ran for two yards on first down, but couldn't hold the snap on second down, which was recovered by teammate Sterling Perkins for a 3-yard loss. Wilson ran again on third down, but Cambridge-SD was flagged for holding.
Wilson's pass on third-and-goal from the 15 was broken up by Colonel's Bradley Thomas. Perkins hauled in Wilson's fourth-down throw but was ruled out of the end zone.
Colonel took over from its 15 with 5:34 remaining. Mitchell ran for nine yards on first down. Ja'Zir Dickerson carried for eight yards and a first down. Three plays later, on third-and-four, Mitchell picked up seven for another first. Dickerson weaved through traffic for 21 yards and a first down. Mitchell then ran for four yards before powering for another tough nine yards and a first down that cemented the win.
"Derrick Mitchell ran the ball hard tonight," Jackson said. "Even at the end of the game, him and Ja'Zir Dickerson had some pretty big runs."
That combination made big plays throughout for Colonel.
Mitchell's 6-yard touchdown run and two-point conversion staked Colonel to an 8-0 lead with 8:50 left in the first quarter.
Cambridge-SD answered, with Perkins scoring on a 4-yard run and Collin Bair booting the point-after to make it 8-7 with 5:11 to go in the first quarter.
Colonel came right back, as Dickerson broke loose for a 65-yard touchdown dash a little over a minute later. Mitchell against ran in the two-point conversion for a 16-7 lead.
On the Vikings' next play from scrimmage, Perkins was sprung for a 63-yard touchdown gallop. Bair's point after pulled Cambridge-SD within 16-14 with 3:56 still left in the first quarter.
Colonel pieced together a 13-play, 69-yard march that culminated with Thomas' 1-yard quarterback sneak and Mitchell's two-point run for a 24-14 lead with 7:43 left in the first half.
Cambridge-SD wouldn't get any closer in the first half, as Twilley was intercepted, first by Zy'arron Nichols midway through the quarter, and then by Dickerson less than 30 seconds before halftime.
Dickerson appeared to lengthen Colonel's lead, when he returned the second-half opening kickoff 80 yards for a touchdown. But a clipping penalty erased that score.
The Viking defense stiffened, forcing a punt. But the snap sailed over punter Jackson Jean's head and Cambridge-SD took over at the Colonel 32. Nine plays later, Perkins slammed in from one yard out, then ran in the two-point conversion, drawing the Vikings within 24-22 with 7:04 left in the third.
Colonel responded, as Thomas found Dickerson in stride on a slant pattern for a 50-yard touchdown and a 30-22 lead with 5:43 to go in the third. Mitchell was stopped on the two-point attempt.
The Vikings again trimmed their deficit as Twilley hit Semaj Pinder for a 3-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-goal with 2:02 remaining in the third. Twilley's two-point pass attempt was broken up by Thomas, keeping the score 30-28.
Mitchell's final touchdown pushed Colonel's lead back to 10.
"They have some resilience," Jackson said of his team. "Our guys didn't quit. They kept fighting. During halftime and before the game we told them they were going to have to grind this out and fight to pull through this game, and they did. They just kept fighting. I couldn't be more proud of them."

 CENTREVILLE — As Queen Anne's County High's boys soccer team prepared for its victory jog across the field Wednesday night, a handful of Lions coaxed head coach Wade Hosler to find a place in line and join the run.Hosler made it halfway across the field then started applauding.
"It's senior night," he said. "Let them have it."
It was also the night Hosler earned his 100th career victory, as Jamison Kendall's first-half goal proved enough in a 1-0 victory over a no-quit North Dorchester bunch, keeping the Lions atop the North Bayside.
"I guess it means I'm getting old," said a smiling Hosler of his milestone. "I didn't really sit down and think about it too much. It's been a lot of tremendous players, a lot of great assistant coaches, administration. A lot of people have helped me along the way.
"It's been an amazing journey," continued Hosler, now in his 13th season at the helm. "We have great kids. They come out and they work hard every year. We graduate good kids, and good kids fill their shoes. So it's a good place to be. If it wasn't I wouldn't have lasted this long."
With their fourth win in five games, the Lions (5-3 overall, 5-0 North Bayside) remained in first place in the division via their fourth one-goal win of the season.
"It's always a little stressful," Hosler said of senior night. "We didn't finish the ball, which makes it difficult. We finish a couple more early (chances) and it would be a different game. But we don't put the ball in the back of the net and it becomes a struggle."
Queen Anne's got four corner-kick chances in the opening 15 minutes but couldn't convert. And though the Lions controlled possession for much of the first half, the Eagles (4-4-1, 1-4-1) found openings and opportunities, the biggest coming with 26 minutes, 18 seconds remaining, when Christian Chase drilled a strike off the crossbar.
The Lions cranked up the intensity on the offensive end, with James Rath sending a pair of shots on goal that North Dorchester keeper Jayden Coleman stopped. But with just under 18 minutes left before half, the Lions worked the ball down the right side and over to Kendall, who steered a left-footed shot past Coleman for a 1-0 lead.
"We had good pressure," Eagles head coach Gabe Guzman said. "It's one of those nights where things don't fall your way and you have to live with the results. Unfortunately, we had one mistake in the back end."
Queen Anne's continued building chances toward padding its lead in the second half. Coleman stopped Trey Moore's header with 27:27 to go. Kendall was denied with 13:30 remaining and Rath unloaded a drive wide left 2 minutes later.
North Dorchester pushed into the Lions end in the final 5 minutes in a bid for the equalizer. Senior captain Chris Sanchez, who booted a number of long clears and balls into the Queen Anne's end throughout the game, drove a direct kick wide left with a little over 5 minutes left. The Eagles got a corner with 3 minutes to go, but couldn't muster a shot.
About a minute later, the Eagles sent a through ball into the box. But Lions sophomore keeper Braeden Livingston sprinted off his line and scooped the ball before anyone else could get a touch.
"It makes it stressful," Hosler said of his team's one-goal wins. "But hey, we're playing well. We're still undefeated in the North. And I'm proud of the way we grind. It's not pretty. We're not finishing as many opportunities as we would like, but we keep grinding. We keep fighting. And we find a way to win."
Guzman also liked his team's fight, and with a little work, hopes to be a force in the Class 1A East playoffs.
"We're still working things out," said Guzman, whose team is 4-1-1 against 1A competition this season. "Finishing is still a little bit of an issue. It's a work in progress. Hopefully come playoff time we won't have that issue.
"Kudos to them," Guzman added of Hosler and Queen Anne's. "Hundredth win. That's a wonderful feat. Hopefully one day I'll be there. But they did their job."

But Corder tweaked her corner design during intermission, then watched Mel Gill set up Jordan Bilbo's back-to-back goals off corners, sparking the Lions to their third straight shutout via a 3-0 victory over the Warriors.
"At halftime we just made up that corner," said Corder after her team improved to 6-2 overall, 3-0 North Bayside. Called it a new name, put it in. It was there every time."
The first time came with 2 minutes, 25 seconds remaining in the third quarter. Bilbo directed an entry pass to Gill, who returned the ball to Bilbo and watched the senior midfielder snap a shot into the back of the cage for a 1-0 lead.
"Our coaches see everything on the field," Bilbo said. "We trust our coaches so much. So when they say we have to make a halftime adjustment, we do it. That was one of our halftime adjustments. And I couldn't have asked for a better pass from my teammate Mel Gill. Everything just fell into place."
Everything fell into place a second time with 9:47 left in the game, as Gill handled the entry pass and returned it Bilbo, who slammed a shot to the left of Easton goalie Taylor Bowen for a two-goal lead.
"I'm just so happy to see it executed on the field," Bilbo said.
So was Corder.
"I'm super glad we got some corner goals today," Corder said. "Mel had a good hold to read the defender to get her to commit and then it was money."
Less than a minute after Bilbo's second strike, Easton head coach Kim Neff called time.
"I wanted to regroup and tell them, 'No matter what the score is we don't give up,'" Neff said. "'We are in this game until the very end.'"
The Warriors didn't fold, but 49 seconds from the end of the game, the Lions bumped the score to 3-0 as Haley Cole swept a backhander into the cage.
"They're a great team," Corder said of Easton, which slipped to 4-3, 1-2. "We had to fight for that. We only gave up one defensive corner, so that's huge. And we pushed our defense really high up for today, just to see if we could get that rush on."

Lions goalie Caroline Kimball, who played the first and third quarters, made her toughest save with 5:22 left in the first quarter, when she stopped a shot by Stella Kabler. Lilah Kennedy played the second and fourth quarter in goal for Queen Anne's.

Per NFL research, the Jackson-Mahomes matchup will be the first between multiple-time MVP QBs in which each enters the game with a losing record that season. It will also be the first matchup between multi-time MVP QBs with a combined record under .500.
Overall, the AFC is off to a poor start.

In the NFC, all seven 2024 playoff teams have winning records plus three other clubs.
It's too early for any team to panic except for the two-time defending AFC South champion Texans (0-3). Houston is in a tough spot with Indianapolis (3-0) and Jacksonville (2-1) both playing well.

ROOKIE BOND
Texans rookie wide receivers Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel became close friends at Iowa State and their tight-knit relationship has only grown stronger since Houston selected Higgins in the second round of the NFL draft and Noel in the third.
The rookies love to fish so they started the "J&JFishinn" TikTok channel in college. They've got bigger priorities right now adjusting to life in the NFL but still plan to go fishing when they can.

Running back Jamier Copper carried 18 times for 133 yards and three touchdowns, quarterback Brady Walls was 10 of 10 passing for 200 yards and a pair of scoring strikes, and Easton scored on all seven of its possession Friday night on the way to a 49-7 victory over North Caroline.
"The focus was to start fast tonight," said Griffith after the Warriors improved to 4-0. "We did that on both sides of the ball. Started fast, kept our momentum going."
Easton needed just three plays to take the lead. Jordan Horsey had runs of 10 and 50 yards before Copper found room around left end for a 4-yard touchdown run. Luke Stanco's point-after kick made 7-0 with 1:04 elapsed off the clock.
After North Caroline (0-4) went three-and-out, Easton took possession at its own 18 and pieced together an 11-play march that was capped by Copper's 6-yard run around right end.
"The o-line did their thing," Copper said of center Jack Chapple, guards TJ Truxton and Brody Gilliece, tackles Xavier Stowers and Tymiere Thomas, and Darrien Downes, who was rotated in throughout the game. "You're not going to get nowhere without the o-line."
Easton stretched its lead to 21-0 with 1:23 remaining in the first quarter, when Carter Mooney caught a Walls strike and battled his way into the end zone for a 31-yard scoring play.
"Offensively we were really good tonight," said Griffith, whose team amassed 432 yards of offense. "We still have a lot of things we can fix and do, but at the end of the day the boys worked hard enough to get (a win).

title: Seahawks slip past Warriors
author: Bill Haufe

Seahawks slip past Warriors

 EASTON — Katie Griffin sensed scoring opportunities were going to be few Wednesday afternoon.So at halftime, Stephen Decatur High's head field hockey coach and her assistants did a little preaching.
"'You guys have to be ready in the circle,'" Griffin said to her team.
Kate Reed was just that at the end of the third quarter, poking in a rebound for the game's lone goal as the Seahawks remained undefeated with a 1-0 victory over Easton.
"I felt like in the first half we were kind of standing up," Griffin said after Decatur improved to 4-0 via its narrowest margin of victory this season. "And when the ball came our way, by the time we got down it was past us. So we really harped at halftime, 'Like you have to be low and ready in the circle at all times. There's no reason why you're standing up in the circle.' I feel like they adjusted. They listened to us. Really proud of their fight today."
Easton head coach Kim Neff was equally proud of the fight her defense put up while suffering its second one-goal loss of the season.
"My defense played a clean game," Neff said of Kadence McGuckin, Sammy Townsend, Hannah Dahlen, Alden Gibbons-Neff and goalie Taylor Bowen. "And they didn't get many calls in that circle, which was great. They were trapping us in the corner and we were able to maneuver out. It was a good team. It was a great game. We just couldn't execute on those few chances we had today."
While Decatur had the ball in Easton's end the majority of the first half, it put little pressure on Bowen. The Warriors (4-2) did earn the first half's lone corner, but couldn't muster a shot on goal.
Decatur picked up its first corner 1 minute, 13 seconds into the third quarter, sending a shot well wide of the cage. Easton failed to get a shot on the cage on its second corner, then had to play down one player after drawing a card. Bowen made a pad save on one shot, then flopped to the ground to stop another Seahawks chance.
The Warriors got their third corner with 2:40 left in the third, but goalie Kate Miller-Vail quickly booted the ball away.
Decatur earned its second — and last — corner just before the third-period horn sounded. Corners have to be played out regardless if there's no time showing on the clock. Bailey Griffin, the coach's daughter, got the ball on the left side of the circle and swept a shot that Bowen made an initial glove save on. But Bowen lost her glove on the play, and Reed quickly knocked the ball into the cage for the game's lone score.
"Kate was just super fast on the rebound," Coach Griffin said. "Without even thinking, she picked it up off the ground in front of her and just shot it into the cage. A great effort by her to be ready."
Reed's goal seemed to stir Easton's offense, as it began pushing more into the Seahawks' end and circle.
"We definitely put the pressure on at the end," Neff said. "I felt like the first half our middies were kind of playing defensively, and at halftime we talked about that; 'We have to be more on the attack.'"
Miller-Vail (five saves) made her first stop of the fourth quarter with 7:38 remaining. Easton was awarded a corner, but steered a shot wide. Sloane Gunshenan hit a shot from right wing that Miller-Vail turned aside with 4 minutes left. The Warriors got one more corner chance with a little over a minute remaining, but the Seahawks quickly cleared.
"Our goalie did a phenomenal job," Katie Griffin said. "And Bailey, with her ability to just get the ball out of our circle and send it down the field and buy us a few minutes of breathing. She really is great at coming up with the ball. But Kate was just a wall back there. She has great clears."
Easton finished with four corners to Decatur's two.
"I think it's so evenly matched that when you have an opportunity, if you don't execute it that could be the game," Neff said. "We had more corners that just didn't pan out today."

"I don't know what we are yet because I haven't seen our ceiling," Hambleton said. "I haven't seen it (for a full) 80 minutes."
Hambleton liked what saw after the first six minutes Monday night, as the Saints fell behind for the first time this season, then rolled to a 4-1 victory over Colonel Richardson.
Though the season has yet to reach its midway point, St. Michaels (4-0-1 overall, 2-0-1 North Bayside) has thrust itself into the early logjam atop division with defending North champion Queen Anne's (2-2, 2-0), North Caroline (2-2, 2-0) and Kent Island (2-2-1, 2-0-1).
"Seeing them answer, I hate to say, it's expected," said Hambleton of his team after Josue Diaz's strike into the upper left corner staked Colonel Richardson (3-2-1, 1-2) to a 1-0 lead 4:32 into the game. "I didn't see anyone deflate. One thing in years past, once we get close competition and we feel like we can outplay 'em, it's an even game. It's 2-1. It's overtime. It's a tie. So our pressure is different.
"These guys can create momentum," Hambleton continued. "Down 1-0 and coming back and getting tied with them. Being up three and still finding the motor to continue the game. They're not even at the peak yet, because we had plenty of mistakes. And we don't come out of the gate gunning. This team you don't have to motivate. It comes natural."
The tying goal came just 2:19 later off a corner, when senior forward Connor Wheeler slid a shot past Colonel keeper Jamie Mensonides (five saves) into the right side of the net.
The Saints were just getting revved up while the Colonels' scoring was done thanks to a St. Michaels defense led by senior captains Johnny Mautz and Tyler Murphy, sophomore Wyatt Genrich and sophomore keeper Lucas Greenwood (five saves).
"I think last year we just let off the gas and we'd just fall back down to our competition and let that eat at us," Wheeler said if the Saints fell behind in 2024. "I think we had that entire momentum throughout the game. We just have that mentality that keeps us going throughout the entire game that let's us go up 4-1."
That momentum has stemmed partly from last year's first-round playoff loss at Colonel Richardson.
"They took that playoff last year personal," Hambleton said of his team. "And that's not motivated this game. It's motivated the entire season."
Mensonides kept it a stalemate, watching Abel Delgaudio's shot roll wide left with 24 minutes left before making a leaping stop on a header with 19:23 to go in the half. But with 16 minutes remaining, a St. Michaels player was taken down in the box, setting up Gavin Bieber's penalty kick into the right corner for a 2-1 Saints lead.
St. Michaels' Brody McDaniel barely missed expanding that lead, when he sent a drive off the left post 14 minutes before halftime. The Saints carried their one-goal edge into the break as Greenwood hit the ground twice over a 22-second span to make saves.
The Saints continued pressuring Mensonides, who punched away a shot at the right post off a corner, only to have Bieber find the loose ball and tuck it into the net for a 3-1 lead with 26:23 left in the game.
That two-goal cushion may have served as a reminder to the Saints, who had a two-goal lead against Kent Island a week earlier before the Bucs rallied for a 2-2 double-overtime draw.
"We learned a lesson," Mautz said. "We were up 2-0 on KI and obviously that wasn't enough with 20 minutes left. We got to put them away until the last second.
"Last year we would play to our comp," said Mautz, echoing Hambleton's sentiments. "I feel like this year we are playing up above thqt. We're playing at where we can play; at an elite level."
Wheeler had an opportunity to further widen the lead, but was called offsides. Less than a minute later, the senior striker again gained possession, and with Colonel's Skyler Endzel closing on his left hip, angled a right-footed shot that glanced off Mensonides' hands and into the left corner of the net for a 4-1 lead a little over 15 minutes remaining.
"We're always taught to keep our foot on their neck and don't stop until that horn goes off," Wheeler said.
Colonel had two chances to cut into its deficit, with Shafay Alvi shooting wide left with 12:40 remaining, and Ludver Vasquez getting denied by Greenwood a little over a minute later.
"I think a big difference was they are more seasoned than us," Colonel head coach Dillon Shaheen said. "That was apparent on their offensive end. They were a little more physical, ran a little more faster, and ultimately were able to get to the ball a little more than we were. The Buccaneers stretched that lead to 10-0, when running back Jaxson Hess caught a short pass from quarterback Trace Klapaska and broke a handful of tackles en route to a 52-yard touchdown 32 seconds before intermission. Chappell added the extra point.
"The speed of the game was really fast, especially for our quarterback and our offensive line," said Griffith, who watched quarterback Brady Walls battle pressure for most of the first half. "They've got a great defense. They play fast, they play hard.
"Tim had a great game plan," Griffith added of Kent Island head coach Tim Goodrich. "We've played each other so many times. He's got a lot of defenses you practice for. So even what they were doing we practice. But you can't simulate how hard and how fast they play. They gave us a helluva time in the first half."
Kent Island put the Warriors in a deeper hole with just under 8 minutes left in the third quarter, when fullback Alex Brestensky busted loose for an 87-yard touchdown jaunt that — together with another Chappell PAT — made it 17-0.
Easton answered.
Three Jamier Copper carries netted 26 yards. Horsey ran for 8 and 5 yards. Walls then connected with Kyree Acree for a 37-yard gain, setting up the first of Horsey's three TD runs, a 3-yard run up the middle. Stanco's first PAT made it 17-7 with 5:33 left in the third quarter.

Easton forced a three-and-out and took possession at its 30 with 4:23 remaining. A 9-yard completion from Walls to Barnhart coupled with a roughing-the-passer penalty on Kent Island, moved the Warriors to Kent Island's 40.
On third-and-10, Walls dumped a short pass to Horsey for a 22-yard pickup. A Walls-to-Mooney connection pushed Easton to the Bucs' 6. Horsey carried for gains of 2 and 3 yards, before launching himself over the goal line from 1 to tie the game at 20-20 with 1:28 left.
"I felt like (NFL Hall of Fame running back) Emmitt Smith jumping over the pile," Horsey said of his tying touchdown.
On came Stanco to convert his third PAT of the game for a 21-20 lead.
"After I made the first (point-after) kick, got the nervousness out," Stanco said. "Then I made the second and we got close. And then the game was on me; game was on the line. I had to put it through the uprights and I did."

 WASHINGTON — The DC Council voted 11-2 Wednesday in favor of constructing a new stadium complex in the nation's capital to once again house the Washington Commanders."Fans of the team can rightly celebrate the return of the Commanders to the district as a major moment in our city's proud history," said Ward 6 Council member Charles Allen.
The resolution authorizes the city to proceed with development plans for a replacement for the Robert F. Kennedy Memorial Stadium, which currently is being demolished.
"The District now has a once-in-a-generation opportunity to continue to revitalize the Anacostia Waterfront…and develop a vibrant, mixed-use development featuring community sports, professional sports, public recreation, public park space, and cultural amenities," the bill stated.
The Robert F. Kennedy Campus Redevelopment Act of 2025 authorizes the "redevelopment and management" of the property, including the construction of a new stadium.
This arena would relocate the Washington Commanders from their current stadium in Landover, where the franchise has played since 1997.
The stadium aspect of the project is scheduled to be completed in December of 2030 while development of the surrounding area is set to be finished in 2040.
The new stadium will have a transparent roof and hold crowds of up to 65,000, just slightly smaller than the Northwest Stadium (formerly FedEx Field) in Landover, which holds 67,617.
The Commanders are contributing at least $2.7 billion to the property's development, as well as the full cost of the stadium's construction, which is estimated to cost below $500 million.
Jurisdiction over the 180-acre property was transferred to the DC Council in January following a decade-long effort to absorb the land from the federal government.
The council also has outlined other plans to develop the property, including building restaurants, retail, and around 5,000 housing units.
This decision marks the first time in nearly three decades in which the Commanders, previously known as the Redskins, will play a home game in the District of Columbia.
The final NFL game played in RFK Stadium took place Dec. 22, 1996. The stadium was used in the following years for other sports events and entertainment. It has been fully closed to the public since 2019.

 EASTON — Jimmy Cohoon suddenly forgot about the pain from his bloodied nose.Funny how scoring the game-winning goal against a big rival will do that.
Tyler Gutierrez sent a free kick into the box that Cohoon chipped into the top of the net with 1 minute, 7 seconds elapsed in the second overtime Monday, lifting North Caroline High's boys soccer team to a 2-1 victory over Easton in a North Bayside clash that could go a long way toward shaping the division title race.
"Credit to Avery (Brice) and Chad (Hutchison)," North Caroline head coach John Austin said of Easton's head and assistant coaches. "I don't know if that's the best they've played all year but, man, they gave us everything we could handle tonight.
"They were the more aggressive team," Austin said of Easton. "They were the more physical team. There were many, many, many points in the game they were the better team. But we're 1-0 in the North. We'll take the win."
The Bulldogs (1-1 overall, 1-0) North) got the win off a set piece a little over a minute into the second 10-minute overtime, when Gutierrez struck a ball from the left wing right in front of the goal and Warrior keeper Sam Hutchison.
"We do it a lot in practice," Cohoon said of the winning set piece. "I like to get up in front of the group on to their last defender, try and draw him up. I just have to keep trying to get in front of him. And the person (Gutierrez) that's taking the free kick hits it at me pretty hard. But that's what I tell him to do. I just try and get my foot on it and get it over the goalie."
Cohoon got enough of his foot on the ball to pop just over Hutchison and into the top right of the net for the game-winner before peeling off and running upfield and toward the Caroline cheering section of the bleachers.
"Jimmy, he did a lot tonight," said Austin of his senior center back, who got his nose bloodied from an inadvertent elbow in the second half. "Between holding my back line — him and Lewis Higgs — basically my whole set piece runs through them. For them to run 120 yards up and down the field on every set piece. … I give a lot of credit to those guys."
Austin also gave a lot of credit to senior keeper Mason Shilling, who made a slew of strong saves, especially in the second half when the Warriors (2-2, 1-1) were pushing for the equalizer.
"He played great," Austin said of Shilling, who had seven saves. "He kept us in the game. Easton was more into us and he made some great saves. He's been everything we've asked for."
North Caroline took a 1-0 lead with 23:30 left in the first half, when Ayden Russell gained possession deep in the left corner and sent a cross into the box that Jonnathan Luna Feliciano one touched into the net.
Shilling made that lead stand, stopping a header, punching away a shot, before falling to his knees for another save, all in a 2-minute, 22-second window early in the second half. Then with 14:05 left in regulation, Kyle Ensminger got taken down in the box, setting up a penalty kick, which he stuck in the left corner to the tie the game at 1-1.
"They are outworking us," Austin told his team heading into the first 10-minute overtime.
The Warriors continued to press, and Shilling continued to deny them, making a stop at the left post on a direct kick in the first minute of the extra session, then coming off his line to make another save a few moments later.
The game moved into a second OT, where Cohoon knocked in the game-winner.
"I told them, 'It's a small margin for mistakes,'" Brice said. "'One play. It just goes back to doing the simple things right. Last play of the game. I know you're fatigued but you've got to move your feet. You can't foul. You can't give a team like that an opportunity to get a ball on frame. And that's all it is.
"I'm just proud of my guys," Brice continued. "We played well tonight. You learn from it and you respond and we move forward. And it's just simple. We don't need to overcomplicate anything right now. But I told them, 'It's a small margin for error. You just can't make those simple mistakes.'"

Secondly, and more importantly for Leventry, Queen Anne's showed a toughness its head coach hopes will carry it through the regular season and into a deep postseason run. One point away from going to a fourth set, the Lions rallied to score the final five points of the third set Thursday night to complete a 25-22, 25-17, 26-24 victory over the Warriors.
"Definitely saw some good things," said Leventry, whose team improved to 2-0 overall, 1-0 North Bayside with its second sweep of the season. "Some things we've been working on are starting to take place."
If one of those things is developing a mental grit, it surfaced at just the right time. Down six points, Easton (1-1, 0-1) had energy on its side as it rallied to take a 24-21 lead in the third set. But two errant returns pulled the Lions within 24-23, prompting an Easton timeout.
Play resumed with Queen Anne's Alli Dill making a kill to even the match at 24-all. The Lions inched ahead at 25-24 when the Warriors' return of Lauryn Hill's serve again found the net, then sealed the win on Sydney Pinder's game-winning put-away.
"The goal of the season is to be able to play at that level consistently," Leventry said. "We started off that way in set three, then kind of had that big letdown, and then luckily we were able to play hard and close it out. Early season volleyball. We're still a little streaky."
Though the Lions swept Easton twice last season en route to a third consecutive Bayside Conference championship, closing out this group of Warriors proved a bit more difficult.
"She's done a fantastic job," Leventry said of Zador, who's played since she was six years old growing up in Argentina, where she competed at the college and club levels. "They pass the ball exceptionally well in serve-receive. They played some great defense. They really have improved. And they're going to keep getting better."
Easton trailed by five three times in the opening set, but closed within 23-22 before a net serve and kill from Queen Anne's standout Bianca Baker cemented the 25-22 win. The second set featured eight ties before Jory Long served the final four points to push the Lions to a 2-0 lead.
"That was a really good team," Zador said of Queen Anne's. "Every single one of them will hit. Every single one of them will block; will cover. And we have so much work to do based on those (things)."
Queen Anne's looked ready to complete the sweep in set three. An early service run from Dill helped the Lions to a quick 4-1 lead. Baker's ace, Hill's spike and consecutive net returns pushed that advantage to 12-6.

A four-point service rally from Neely Byrnes that included Camryn Webb's kill and a long Lions return, knotted the match at 12-all. Kent Island (1-1) took the opening kickoff and drove from its 25-yard line to the Knights' 3, where it settled for a 20-yard Spencer Chappell field goal with 6 minutes, 41 seconds remaining in the first quarter for a 3-0 lead.
The Bucs maintained that lead until early in the second quarter, when Middletown running back Ryan McLister was sprung for a 31-yard gain, setting up quarterback Brittin Poffenbarger's 3-yard touchdown run off left guard. Ryan Coulby's point-after kick made it 7-3 with 8:15 left in the half.

Queen Anne's capped the regular-season slate by tying Kent Island in another 1v1 showdown, then edged the Bucs 1-0 for a second consecutive Class 2A East Region I title. "I'm just very, very excited," Kent Island head coach Laura Harding said. "Hopefully we go far in the playoffs. I have high expectations for our team."
